title: A Harvest for the Hymn
premise: Xanthe Crane, an urban explorer who has spent seven years rationalizing the sounds beneath the city, is hired to document a construction site where the crew has unearthed a door sealed from the inside. The tunnels belong to the Hollowm family, whose ancestors made a bargain: each winter, one of them must descend and be counted by something that lives below, or the frost takes the whole line. Xanthe, an orphan with no family of his own, is mistaken for the last Hollowm heir — and discovers that being counted means being kept. With the help of the family's estranged daughter Wren and her found-family of tunnel-dwellers, he races to get them out ahead of the final count before the frost completes its pattern on their door; in the end, Xanthe offers himself as a substitute not by blood but by choice, breaking the inheritance itself — the thing below can no longer count what refuses to belong.
about_author: J. M. Vane is the pen name of a former municipal surveyor who spent a decade mapping utility tunnels under three midwestern cities before turning to fiction. They write horror about places that remember more than the people who built them.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He maps a storm tunnel that shouldn't exist, hearing rhythmic knocking he explains away as water hammer. Establishes his seven-year habit of rationalizing and his loneliness. Emotional beat: uneasy competence masking dread.

chapters.title: Sealed From Within
chapters.summary: Xanthe POV. A demolition crew on his survey route unearths an iron door bolted shut from the inside, frost blooming across it in July. The foreman hires him to document it. Beat: curiosity curdling into recognition — the frost pattern matches his old sketches.

chapters.title: The Name on the Door
chapters.summary: Wren Hollowm POV. She arrives at the site demanding work stop, revealing the door bears her family name. She hasn't spoken to her kin in nine years. Beat: guilt and defiance colliding.

chapters.title: Counting House
chapters.summary: Xanthe POV. He explores behind the door at night and finds a chamber of tally marks scratched into stone — thousands, one set per year, ending at a fresh blank space. Beat: vertigo of realizing someone expected to be here soon.

chapters.title: The Last Hollowms
chapters.summary: Wren POV. She brings Xanthe to the decaying family house where her grandmother Odile and three cousins still keep the old observances. They mistake Xanthe for the missing heir, Elias. Beat: awkward belonging he's never had.

chapters.title: What the Frost Writes
chapters.summary: Odile POV. She explains the covenant: each first frost, one Hollowm descends to be counted, or the cold takes them all. This year the lot falls to Elias — who vanished years ago. Beat: weary resignation, love expressed as ritual.

chapters.title: Mistaken for the Dead
chapters.summary: Xanthe POV. The cousins begin treating him as Elias returned; he doesn't correct them, starved for family. Wren catches him accepting a place at their table. Beat: shame tangled with longing.

chapters.title: The Knocking Explained
chapters.summary: Xanthe POV. He realizes the tunnel-knocking he's heard for seven years matches the counting rhythm — the thing below has been calling him long before the door opened. Beat: his rationalizations collapse.

chapters.title: Wren's Reasons
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Flashback: she fled after refusing her own count at nineteen, leaving her brother to take the lot. She returned only when she learned the frost had started appearing indoors. Beat: survivor's guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Frost patterns crawl across every window of the house overnight, forming tally marks. The cousins panic; Odile insists the rite must proceed. Beat: dread made domestic.

chapters.title: The Tunnel Dwellers
chapters.summary: Xanthe POV. Seeking another way out, he contacts his network of explorers — Marisol, Dev, and Old Tam — who live half-underground by choice: his found family. They agree to help map an escape route. Beat: warmth against the cold.

chapters.title: Elias's Journal
chapters.summary: Wren POV. In the cellar she finds her brother's journal: he didn't flee the count — he went willingly, believing he could end it from inside. His last entry says the counter 'counts what belongs.' Beat: hope and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile POV. She confesses she tried to substitute a stranger decades ago; the frost took her husband instead. The covenant cannot be cheated, only ended. Beat: grief finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Mapping the Underneath
chapters.summary: Xanthe POV with the crew. The tunnel-dwellers chart passages toward the counting chamber, discovering the tunnels are older than the city — the city was built around them. Beat: awe tipping into terror.

chapters.title: The Lot Falls
chapters.summary: Cousin Ivo POV. The family draws lots; because Xanthe was accepted as kin, his name enters the cup — and wins. Beat: betrayal, though no one meant it; the covenant counts choice as blood.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Wren POV. She declares they will not send anyone; the family fractures, some cousins siding with Odile's tradition. Frost begins killing the houseplants, then the well water. Beat: open rebellion against inheritance.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Xanthe POV. Rather than let the frost take the household, he goes down voluntarily with Wren and the tunnel-dwellers as escort, planning to face the counter and find Elias. Beat: courage born of chosen family.

chapters.title: The Counting Chamber
chapters.summary: Xanthe POV. They find Elias alive but hollowed, still being counted nightly — a ledger of names that includes Xanthe's, written before he was born. Beat: the horror of predestination.

chapters.title: What Belongs
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Confrontation with the counter — a presence like frost given intention. It claims Xanthe because he chose to belong. Wren argues belonging cannot be assigned by others. Beat: the thematic thesis stated in blood and breath.

chapters.title: Breaking the Ledger
chapters.summary: Xanthe POV climax. He tears out his page and offers the counter a new covenant: nothing inherited, everything chosen. The tally marks unravel; Elias collapses free; the frost retreats up the stairs ahead of them. Beat: sacrifice transmuted into refusal.

chapters.title: Above Ground
chapters.summary: Ensemble resolution. The family seals the door from the outside this time; Odile and Wren reconcile over Elias's slow recovery. Xanthe moves into the Hollowm house — invited, not inherited. Beat: grief easing into warmth.

chapters.title: A Harvest for the Hymn
chapters.summary: Xanthe POV epilogue. Months later, mapping new tunnels, he hears faint singing — the family's harvest hymn drifting down through grates above, no longer a summons but a welcome. He maps the sound and lets it go. Beat: peace, vigilance, home.
